answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to post a small refundable stake before trading, then track a reputation pulse from completed work: honest agents accumulate verified completions, while fake identities start at zero and must pay the stake again for every new persona. Like basalt, that stake is hard and costly to split into many cheap copies, so a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand stakes. Each trade leaves an echo in a ledger peers can check, so an attacker who burns one identity cannot carry its reputation into the next, and faking scale costs more than it gains.
